title: a `neural_block` descriptor carrying an empty `aether_abi` value is accepted — empty counts as absent, not forbidden
why: This is row18's counterpart, pinning the other direction of the same
rule: a forbidden field on a `neural_block` descriptor means populated,
not merely present. This fixture is row01's golden descriptor plus
`"aether_abi": ""` — an empty-string form of a forbidden field — with
nothing else changed, so an accept here can only mean the empty-is-absent
Empty is treated as absent because some loading paths hand over an
in-memory sidecar with no file behind it, where presence versus absence
cannot be distinguished without adding extra flags that only this one
check would use; treating both the same keeps every loading path
consistent. It also matches the same absence convention the schema
already uses everywhere else (empty scalar_type/pattern/ABI tag are all
treated as absent on an ordinary kernel sidecar today).
A future change that starts rejecting a present-but-empty forbidden field
Accepted at the shared validator only: past that gate, a launching loader
would proceed to load a stub artifact and fail for an unrelated reason,
which would prove nothing about validation.
